title: The Six Shooter
paragraphs: Adult western drama starring James Stewart as Britt Ponset. The GRH container includes the July 1953 sales audition, all 39 regular NBC episodes, one exact duplicate collection copy of episode 30, and three short editorial/reference tracks; the April 1952 Hollywood Star Playhouse precursor is documented historically but is not preserved here as a full broadcast object.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: NBC regular run (September 20, 1953 to June 24, 1954) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Basil Adlam (music, composer, and conductor), Jack Johnstone (director, performer, and producer), James Stewart (performer), Jimmy Stewart (performer), Frank Burt (creator and writer), Hal Gibney (announcer and host), and John Wald (announcer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]].

The stories often return to frontier western setting and culture, wandering gunfighter and outsider protagonist, frontier justice, law and moral choice, family loyalty and kinship, robbery, outlaw crime and pursuit, and revenge and cycles of violence.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Hollywood Star Playhouse precursor to a regular series, Adult western drama in late network radio, James Stewart film-western persona carried into radio, and Brief commercial sponsorship followed by sustaining broadcasts.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|broadway-is-my-beat|Broadway Is My Beat]], [[show|escape|Escape]], and [[show|the-railroad-hour|The Railroad Hour]].
